title: Sub-minimum sample counts and skipped estimators are invisible in the JSON report (errorLevel stays 0)
body:
## Summary

Two related gaps in the JSON report make a degraded run indistinguishable from a compliant one:

1. **Sub-minimum sample counts.** §3.1.1 requires at least 1,000,000 samples. `non_iid_main.cpp` prints `*** Warning: data contains less than 1000000 samples ***` to stdout and continues; `errorLevel` is set to 0 and `test_run_base.h` emits `errorMessage` only when `errorLevel != 0`, so the JSON of a 2,000-sample run has `"errorLevel": 0` and no message.
2. **Skipped estimators.** Any estimator that returns −1 ("could not run": compression with ≤ 1000 blocks, MultiMCW below 4096 samples, t-tuple with no 35-fold repeat, LRS with v < u, …) is dropped from the minimum by the `if (ret >= 0)` guards; its JSON test case is emitted as `{"testCaseDesc": …}` with no value, `errorLevel` stays 0, and the reported minimum is over fewer estimators than §6.2 requires ("the minimum of all the estimates").

## Reproduction

Built at `87c104d` (macOS, Apple clang + libomp; `selftest` agrees with `refdata` to 3.7e-10).

```
python3 -c "import random;r=random.Random(777);P=3000;p=[r.randrange(2) for _ in range(P)];open('p2000.bin','wb').write(bytes(p[i%P] for i in range(2000)))"
./ea_non_iid -q -o o.json p2000.bin
#   stdout: *** Warning: data contains less than 1000000 samples ***
#           *** Warning: not enough samples to run compression test (need more than 1000) ***
#           *** Warning: not enough samples to run multiMCW test (need more than 4096) ***
#   o.json: "errorLevel": 0, no "errorMessage";
#           "Compression Test (for bit strings only)" and "Multi Most Common in Window Test" test cases carry no value
./ea_non_iid -vv p2000.bin
#   Assessed min entropy: 0.61486314415516563
```

The same period-3000 source at 1,000,000 samples:

```
./ea_non_iid -vv p1e6.bin        # Assessed min entropy: 1.2912892207571696e-06
```

So a 2,000-sample run of a source whose compliant assessment is ~1e-6 reports 0.61 bit/sample, with the same exit status and the same JSON shape as a compliant run. Nothing in the JSON says the sample count was below the minimum or that two estimators did not contribute to the minimum.

## Request

Set a machine-readable warning/`errorLevel` in the JSON when (a) the sample count is below the §3.1.1 minimum and (b) any estimator returned −1 and was excluded from the minimum — or refuse outright in case (a). Related, not duplicate: #238 asks for the sample count and symbol count in the JSON, which would help a consumer detect (a) but not (b).

Found while auditing this tool for a downstream use that prices output length on the reported min-entropy figure.
